title: Extension of natural comparisons out of a localized functor
statement: Let C,D be categories, W a morphism property of C with right calculus of fractions (identities, composition, right Ore squares and right cancellation refinements), and P a predicate on objects of C. Assume every X admits s:R→X in W with P(R). Let A,B:C→D be functors, with A(s) invertible for s∈W. Suppose α_X:A(X)→B(X) is given for objects satisfying P, and A(t)≫α_Y=α_X≫B(t) for every t:X→Y between such objects. Then there is a natural transformation β:A→B with β_X=α_X for every object satisfying P. No preservation of weak equivalences is assumed for B.

source.place: Resolving-class descent of a comparison from representatives; proved using the right Ore axiom of Stacks Tag 04VC and explicit cancellation.

proof.text: For every X choose a resolution s_X:R_X→X with P(R_X) and s_X∈W. Define β_X=A(s_X)⁻¹≫α_R_X≫B(s_X). Multiplying by A(s_X) gives its defining equation.
Given t:R→X with P(R), apply the right Ore axiom (Stacks 04VC, RMS2) to t and s_X, then resolve the resulting common source. Obtain a:R'→R in W and b:R'→R_X with P(R') and a≫t=b≫s_X.

Apply A to that equality and use naturality of α along a and b, together with the defining equation for β_X. Cancel the isomorphism A(a). This gives A(t)≫β_X=α_R≫B(t) for every arrow t out of a resolving object.

For f:X→Y precompose the desired naturality square with the invertible A(s_X), and apply the preceding formula to s_X and s_X≫f. The same formula at the identity of an object satisfying P gives β_X=α_X.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_natTrans_from_resolvingClass
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D]
    (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    (P : C → Prop)
    (hres : ∀ X : C, ∃ (R : C) (s : R ⟶ X), P R ∧ W s)
    (A B : C ⥤ D) (hA : W.IsInvertedBy A)
    (α : ∀ X : C, P X → (A.obj X ⟶ B.obj X))
    (hα : ∀ (X Y : C) (hX : P X) (hY : P Y) (s : X ⟶ Y),
      A.map s ≫ α Y hY = α X hX ≫ B.map s) :
    ∃ β : A ⟶ B, ∀ (X : C) (hX : P X), β.app X = α X hX
